title: plugin-auth: `no_sign_in_account_at_boot` still fires at ERROR on hosted kernels whose platform-SSO button is hidden (the owner signs in through the cloud handoff, which the gate cannot see)
body:
Filing gate: ① (product defect with a named landing spot; `finding`, class a, `reach:` a named real producer).
Reader: the triage seat routes it on first touch (the gate is in `plugin-auth`, `domain:services`). The executing lane then decides the fix shape.
Dedupe: semantic issue search `no_sign_in_account_at_boot false error delegated sign-in path host handoff SSO` on objectstack returned 2 hits, both closed: #15074 (the parent, below) and #9653 (unrelated). The same on cloud with `platform_sso_enabled hidden sign-in button owner handoff` returned 2 hits: cloud#2437 (the source) and cloud#1683 (unrelated).

## What is wrong

#15074 was fixed by `2c87a48f` (PR #17941): the boot report is suppressed when `getPublicConfig()` shows a delegated sign-in path, meaning `ssoEnforced`, a non-empty `socialProviders`, or enterprise SSO with an IdP row. On a hosted cloud kernel that path is normally the platform-SSO OIDC provider (`objectstack-cloud`), and the report is correctly quiet there. objectstack-ai/cloud PR #2504 pins that case.

One population is still reported falsely: environments whose owner used the cloud console action **"Hide ObjectStack Sign-in"** (`disable_platform_sso`, `packages/service-tenant/src/objects/sys-environment.object.ts` in objectstack-ai/cloud, which writes `platform_sso_enabled = false`).
- The action only hides the login-page button. Its own description says env-native login is unaffected.
- The hosted kernel then wires no `oidcProviders`.
- The owner still enters through the cloud handoff (`sso_as_owner` → `sso-handoff-issue` → `sso-exchange` in cloud's `auth-proxy-plugin.ts`). That path never writes a `sys_account` row.
- So an SSO-only owner (a `sys_user` row, zero `sys_account` rows) on such an environment makes every kernel rebuild log `ERROR [auth] no_sign_in_account_at_boot: … NOBODY CAN SIGN IN, and the deployment CANNOT BE RECOVERED FROM INSIDE …`, while the owner signs in normally. That is the #15074 harm (a false ERROR that drowns real alerts), on a smaller population.

reach: named producer, the console action above. Measured by the cloud#2437 dev at framework `4b4ee88f`: with `platform_sso_enabled` false in the hosted-kernel e2e harness, the rebuild logs the ERROR line above (the mutation leg of cloud PR #2504's test: 3 failed / 1 passed). The number of environments with the button hidden is NOT MEASURED (no control-plane access).

## Where the fix sits

The gate's `SignInPathWiring` has no fact a host can use to declare a delegated sign-in path that is not a login-page provider. The candidate shape, for the executing lane to confirm: let the host declare that humans reach this deployment through a host-owned handoff, and treat that like the other delegated paths.
- ⛔ Not a cloud-side workaround (log filtering or a level override).
- ⛔ Not re-registering a hidden provider just to satisfy the gate: that would make the public config lie about what the login page offers.

## Source

objectstack-ai/cloud#2437 item 2, re-check report 5911753456 on that card; objectstack-ai/cloud PR #2504. Filed by the `repo:cloud` seat (`repo:cloud#1`, session `session_01YSygzqVmrY31BnZge8KDo6`).
